newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Vietnam leads ASEAN growth table - UN unit.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam leads ASEAN growth table - UN unit.

text.p: Vietnam's economic growth should average 9.9 percent annually between 1996 and 2000, ahead of other ASEAN members, the Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) said on Wednesday.
A table of forecasts in the United Nations-affiliated commission's 1997 survey put Malaysia's average gross domestic product (GDP) growth in the period at 8.3 percent and Thailand's at 7.3 percent.
Indonesia and the Philippines were both at seven percent with Singapore just behind at 6.7 percent.
Indonesia had the highest forecast average inflation rate, 9.5 percent, through 1999 using GDP deflators.
Through 1999 and using gross national product deflators, Thailand's average inflation rate was forecast at 4.7 percent and Malaysia's at 2.4 percent.
Through 2000 the inflation rate for Vietnam was projected at 8.8 percent, the Philippines at 6.2 percent and Singapore's at 2.5 percent.
The ESCAP table gave no figures for Brunei, the other member of the Association of South East Asian Nations.

ESCAP said economic growth in southeast Asia had been supported by high rates of domestic investment and savings, and government policies and attitudes "generally have been what is often referred to as business-friendly."
The report said, "All the elements usually advanced as conducive to successful economic growth have been present in the economies of these countries."
